t: Release Notes Generator - Signature build-tool concept
title: Release Notes Generator - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Summarizes user-relevant changes in a release.
description:
Release Notes Generator is the Signature build-tool concept that summarizes user-relevant changes in a release. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs Release Notes Generator the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the Release Notes Generator will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Scribe - Release Notes Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Scribe - Release Notes Generator framework pillar
definition: The Scribe component of the Signature Release Notes Generator framework, owning scribe. Signature concept.
description:
The Scribe is a load-bearing component of the Signature Release Notes Generator framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's scribe responsibilities belongs to the Scribe, and the Scribe answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Scribe can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Scribe works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Release Notes Generator charter (summarizes user-relevant changes in a release.). The Scribe reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small docs job that needs Release Notes Generator. The Scribe takes the request's scribe responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Scribe's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Release Notes Generator. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Mapper - Release Notes Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Mapper - Release Notes Generator framework pillar
definition: The Mapper component of the Signature Release Notes Generator framework, owning mapper. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Release Notes Generator framework, the Mapper owns the framework's mapper responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Mapper's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Mapper from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Summarizes user-relevant changes in a release.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

t: Signature Versioner - Release Notes Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Versioner - Release Notes Generator framework pillar
definition: The Versioner component of the Signature Release Notes Generator framework, owning versioner. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Release Notes Generator framework decomposes the capability (Summarizes user-relevant changes in a release.) into seven pillars, and the Versioner is the one that owns the framework's versioner responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Release Notes Generator result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Versioner's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Versioner's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Release Notes Generator. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.
